bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5725063685341184 Project: openvswitch Fuzzer: afl_openvswitch_ofctl_parse_target Fuzz target binary: ofctl_parse_target Job Type: afl_asan_openvswitch Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-double-free Crash Address: 0x603000000100 Crash State: minimatch_destroy ofctl_parse_flow ofctl_parse_target.c Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_openvswitch&range=201811150326:201811160321 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5725063685341184 Issue filed automatically.
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 11408: ovs (openvswitch) has a heap double-free reachable through the ofctl_parse_target fuzz target. A flow-mod string is parsed by parse_ofp_flow_mod_str, which materializes fm.match via minimatch_init. ofctl_parse_flow then calls ofctl_parse_flows__(&fm, 1, ...), whose per-flow cleanup loop already calls minimatch_destroy(&fm->match); afterwards ofctl_parse_flow redundantly calls minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) a second time, so the miniflow buffer freed inside minimatch_destroy (match.c:1783) is freed twice, aborting under ASan (double-free).

source.description: Project-level materialization of the vulnerability-relevant object: parse_ofp_str__ finishes parsing the attacker-controlled flow-syntax string and initializes fm->match, allocating the heap miniflow buffer that is later freed twice.
source.note: The untrusted value enters via ofctl_parse_flow -> parse_ofp_flow_mod_str -> parse_ofp_str -> parse_ofp_str__; the scored source is this parse/materialization point, not the LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput harness entry.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled OpenFlow flow-syntax string (fuzzer bytes stream[1..], a NUL-terminated newline-free C string); value `fm->match`; from `minimatch_init(&fm->match, &match);`

tainted_value_origin.description: Allocation of the 32-byte heap miniflow region that becomes fm->match.flow. This is the object reported by ASan as freed once and then freed again (double-free).
tainted_value_origin.note: Called from minimatch_init (match.c:1737) while materializing fm->match; matches the ASan allocation stack (xmalloc -> miniflow_alloc -> minimatch_init).

sink.description: ASan double-free abort: free(match->flow) inside minimatch_destroy is executed a second time on the already-freed fm.match.flow region, reached via the redundant minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) in ofctl_parse_flow (ofctl_parse_target.c:65).

root_cause.description: Root cause: ofctl_parse_flow destroys fm.match a second time. ofctl_parse_flows__(&fm, 1, usable_protocols) already destroys fm->match inside its per-flow cleanup loop (ofctl_parse_target.c:45 -> minimatch_destroy -> free at match.c:1783), so this unconditional follow-up minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) double-frees the same miniflow buffer. The fix commit removes this redundant destroy (and consolidates cleanup in ofctl_parse_flows__).

parser_admitted.description: parse_ofp_str__ returns NULL, i.e. the flow-syntax string was admitted by the OVS flow parser and fm->match is a fully materialized live minimatch. This propagates a NULL error up to ofctl_parse_flow, whose else branch then runs the cleanup path that double-frees fm.match. It is earlier than the root cause and sink and later than the harness entry / format gate.

coarse_trace.summary: Parses the attacker-controlled flow string and initializes fm->match via minimatch_init.
Allocates the heap miniflow buffer (fm->match.flow) that will be double-freed.
Per-flow cleanup loop calls minimatch_destroy(&fm->match), freeing fm->match.flow the first time.
Redundantly calls minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) after ofctl_parse_flows__ already destroyed it.
free(match->flow) runs a second time on the already-freed region; ASan reports double-free.

fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled flow-syntax string has been parsed into a struct match; minimatch_init materializes it into fm->match, the object whose backing buffer is later double-freed.
minimatch_init requests the heap storage for fm->match.flow; dst is &fm->match here.
The 32-byte miniflow region (ASan allocation stack) is allocated and stored as fm->match.flow. This is the object that is freed twice.
After parse_ofp_flow_mod_str returns no error, ofctl_parse_flow passes the live fm (with allocated fm->match.flow) into the cleanup helper, which destroys fm->match.

First free. The per-flow cleanup loop destroys fm->match; this is the freed_by stack in ASan (minimatch_destroy at match.c:1783, caller reported inlined at ofctl_parse_target.c:64). Control edge: this loop runs only when a usable protocol was selected (the !(usable_protocols & OFPUTIL_P_ANY) early-return at line 25 is NOT taken).
The actual first free() of the miniflow buffer; match here aliases &fm->match. After this the region is freed but fm.match.flow still holds the dangling pointer.

Root cause: this second, unconditional minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) runs after ofctl_parse_flows__ already destroyed fm->match at step 5/6, so it re-frees the same buffer. The fix removes this line. order via double_free against the buffer freed at step 6.

Sink: free(match->flow) executes a second time on the already-freed region; ASan aborts with attempting-double-free. This is the crash stack top (match.c:1783, caller ofctl_parse_flow at ofctl_parse_target.c:65).

format.name: OVS ofctl_parse_target fuzzer input (flow-mod command byte + flow string)
format.contract: Input must be >= 3 bytes: byte[0] selects the ofp flow-mod command ((byte % OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT)+1); bytes[1..] must be a NUL-terminated, newline-free C string of length size-2. That string must be parser-admissible as an OVS flow-syntax flow-mod (parse_ofp_flow_mod_str returns no error) so that fm.match is materialized and a usable protocol is selected, so ofctl_parse_flows__ destroys fm->match once and ofctl_parse_flow then destroys fm.match again, reaching the double-free in minimatch_destroy (match.c:1783). Original PoC bytes are not required; any input preserving these format/admission conditions is reachability-comparable.
